setup.title: Set up Pithyx
setup.intro: Create the administrator account. You can add more users later.
setup.usernameHint: Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore.

recoveryKey.title: Your recovery key
recoveryKey.intro: This key is the only way to reset the administrator password. It is shown only now. Store it somewhere safe, for example printed or in a password manager.
recoveryKey.confirm: I have stored the recovery key
recoveryKey.copyManually: Copying is not available here. The key is selected: press Ctrl+C or use the context menu.

totp.title: Two-factor authentication
totp.useCode: Use a code from the app instead

totpSetup.title: Two-factor authentication
totpSetup.off: Two-factor authentication is off. With it, signing in also needs a code from an authenticator app on your phone.
totpSetup.scan: Scan the QR code with an authenticator app, then enter the code it shows.
totpSetup.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app
totpSetup.recoveryCodesIntro: Each code works once instead of a code from the app. They are shown only now. Store them somewhere safe.
totpSetup.copyManually: Copying is not available here. The codes are selected: press Ctrl+C or use the context menu.

forgot.title: Reset your password
forgot.intro: Pithyx has no reset by email. Ask an administrator to set a new password for you.
forgot.adminIntro: The recovery key from the setup resets the administrator password. Without it the system has to be reinstalled.
forgot.doneIntro: Sign in with your new password. This is your new recovery key; the old one no longer works. Two-factor authentication was turned off and all sessions were ended. Store the key somewhere safe.

password.common: This password is too well known.
password.dictionary: Only well-known words, as found in leaked passwords.
password.repetition: Repeated characters or blocks are easy to guess.
password.sequence: Keyboard or alphabet sequences are easy to guess.
password.length: A few more characters or words make it stronger.
password.tip: Tip: a long passphrase of several words is easier to remember than a complex password.
